advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether `$rc` at the classifier call site can ever carry 124/137/139; if not, wire the classifier to the actual process/signal status (or document that pytest masks it) so the SIGKILL/SIGSEGV/timeout branches are reachable.
evidence: _build-and-test.yml:852-856: `pytest -m "$DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS" ... || rc=$?` — rc holds pytest's exit code, not the shell 128+signal convention
scripts/classify_runner_exit.py:8-12: `_FAILURE_CAUSES = {124:..., 137: 'SIGKILL...', 139: 'SIGSEGV...'}` keyed on shell signal statuses that the pytest wrapper never propagates as its own exit code
Commit message claims the classifier 'names SIGKILL, SIGSEGV, and timeout statuses in logs' — but pytest's exit code masks the worker signal so those branches stay dead at this call site
advisory.finding: The runner-exit classifier is invoked in CI with pytest's own exit code (`$rc` captured from the `pytest ... || rc=$?` line), not a shell 128+signal status, so the SIGKILL(137)/SIGSEGV(139)/timeout(124) branches that are the stated purpose of the script will essentially never match. A worker killed by OOM/segfault surfaces to the parent `pytest` process as exit code 1 (tests failed), so the classifier prints the generic 'failure: runner exited with status 1' rather than naming the signal.

evidence: _crash_guard.py IS the unit under test (its behavior is exercised by the nested-run tests), so grepping its source text is source-grepping, not a structural grep on an instruction artifact. Rule 4: renaming an internal or editing a comment to contain 'node down' would break this test with zero behavior change.
tests/unit/test_crash_guard.py:69 `assert "test_other_test_passes" not in combined or "rebar crash guard" in combined`

tests/unit/test_crash_guard.py:68 `assert completed.returncode != 0, combined` is the only real masking check; the following disjunction adds nothing because `"rebar crash guard" in combined` is already asserted true in the sibling test and holds whenever escalation occurs.

Regression blindness (Criterion d): if the guard regressed so a crash beside green tests exited 0, only the returncode assert would catch it; the disjunction would still pass, so it cannot detect the named incident (green outcomes beside vanished ones).
advisory.finding: test_crash_guard_uses_xdist_hook_not_output_scraping asserts on the TEXT and AST of the unit under test (tests/_crash_guard.py) rather than its behavior: `assert "node down" not in text.lower()` and `assert "worker crashed" not in text.lower()` are source-grep absence checks over the implementation, and the function-name AST check breaks on a behavior-preserving rename. These break on a comment/wording change with no observable-behavior change.
